Frequently Asked Questions

Our Taylors ranch still has its original ductwork. Should new equipment reuse it?

Only after testing says it can. Original mid-century ducts often leak at seams, lack insulation, and were sized for different equipment entirely, and new systems inherit every one of those problems. A duct evaluation before replacement determines whether sealing, modification, or new runs protect the investment.

How disruptive is repiping an occupied house?

Less than most homeowners expect. Supply repiping typically runs a few days, water stays on each evening, and access openings are planned and patched as part of the job. The disruption of scheduled repiping consistently beats the unscheduled version a burst original line delivers.

Can my older panel handle a modern HVAC replacement?

The evaluation answers it before the install does. New equipment draw gets totaled against the panel’s documented capacity, and most replacements fit, but marginal panels get identified up front so the electrical work is planned rather than discovered on install day.

What is that persistent gurgle after my tub drains?

Gurgling means air is pulling through the trap, usually because a partial blockage or venting problem is starving the drain. It tends to precede a full clog rather than follow one. Trap and pipe cleaning resolves the common version, and a stubborn recurrence means a video inspection is likely the best diagnostic next step.

Which nearby communities do your Taylors routes cover?

Greer, Travelers Rest, and Duncan all sit on adjoining routes. The chat team can confirm any address between them in minutes.
